text:
Predicates:
Engaged(x) ::: x is engaged.
Invite(x, y) ::: x invites y to their ceremony.
MakeWeddingPlans(x) ::: x makes wedding plans.
WellAttendedWedding(x) ::: x has a well-attended wedding.
LargerFamily(x) ::: x has a larger family.
HasWedding(x) ::: x has a wedding.
Question: Is John engaged? 

Premises:
∀x (MakeWeddingPlans(x) → Engaged(x)) ::: All people who make wedding plans are people who are engaged.
∀x (Invite(x, y) → MakeWeddingPlans(x)) ::: All people who invite others make wedding plans.
∀x (WellAttendedWedding(x) → Invite(x, y)) ::: Anyone with a well-attended wedding invites others.
∀x (LargerFamily(x) → (HasWedding(x) ∨ Invite(x, y))) ::: If someone has a larger family, then they either have a well-attended wedding or invite others.
If(Engaged(John), ¬Invite(John, y) ∧ MakeWeddingPlans(John)) ::: If John is engaged, then John does not invite friends and makes wedding plans.
If(LargerFamily(John), then (HasWedding(John) ∨ Invite(John, y))) ::: If John has a larger family, then he either has a well-attended wedding or invites friends.

Conclusion:
Is(Engaged(John))
